extracted.intended_audience: readers, editors, textual scholars of Edgar Allan Poe; Project Gutenberg users/distributors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and practical criteria for selecting, attributing, formatting, and presenting 19th‑century poems (here: Poe), plus Project Gutenberg redistribution/licensing requirements. Useful for editors curating editions and distributors publishing the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of 'Poems written in Youth' material
rubrics_metrics.description: Which pieces to include in the 'Poems written in Youth' section: includes the pieces printed for the first volume of 1827 (suppressed), such poems from the first and second published volumes of 1829 and 1831 as have not already been given in their revised versions, and a few others collected from various sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note 30 explains editorial scope: include original early issues (even from suppressed volumes) and other non-revised pieces as collected. When a later edition introduced additional lines that were omitted in subsequent collections, document that history (example: 'Al Aaraaf' and its prefatory lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Version selection / preference for original or manuscript readings
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial preference may be given to earlier or more 'original' manuscript versions rather than later printed revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note 31 and the annotation for 'Alone' state the editor has sometimes 'taken liberty' to replace a book version with an earlier, perhaps more original manuscript version. Weigh originality/authenticity of manuscripts against later authorial revisions and explicitly state when an earlier version is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and presentation choices (punctuation, indentation, visual appearance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typographical and layout choices (punctuation, indentation, line arrangement) affect readability and perceived quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note 31 remarks that the 'present draft... is more carefully punctuated, and, the lines being indented, presents a more pleasing appearance, to the eye at least.' Editors should consider punctuation and indentation for both fidelity and visual appeal, and record when such choices depart from earlier printings or manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and authenticity standards for doubtful works
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and evidentiary standards to attribute poems to the author (here, Poe) when authorship is uncertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor should seek external proofs (e.g., provenance, facsimile copies, corroborating documentation). If such proofs are not forthcoming, rely on internal evidence (stylistic, linguistic) cautiously. The notes explain restraint where 'proofs were not forthcoming' and reliance on 'internal evidence' to guide inclusion; explicitly mark works as doubtful when evidence is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handwriting and facsimile evidence handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of facsimile handwriting to known samples is a criterion in assessing authorship authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes describe that facsimile copies alleged to be Poe's handwriting differed substantially from many known specimens and resembled handwriting of another contributor; editors should compare handwriting with known exemplars and disclose discrepancies affecting attribution judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of anonymous or pseudonymous publications
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat works that originally appeared unsigned or under noms de plume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notes on 'To Isadore' outline that poems published under names like 'A. Ide, junior' or 'A. M. Ide' may have been pseudonymous. Editors should consider the possibility of the author using pseudonyms (especially when he did so elsewhere), include the pieces where plausible, but annotate and explain the attribution uncertainty to let readers judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in editorial interventions and variant reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should document and explain textual variants, omissions, and editorial interventions (what was omitted, added, or replaced and why).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notes section gives examples: lines originally prefixed to 'Al Aaraaf' that were omitted later, and commentary about versions and suppressed volumes. The editor must provide explanatory notes about variant readings, suppression, and reasons for choosing one reading over another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion policy for 'doubtful' poems (present for reader judgment)
rubrics_metrics.description: When authorship is doubtful but possible, include the pieces in a 'doubtful' section and provide contextual notes so readers can judge authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'DOUBTFUL POEMS' section and its Notes explain the practice of including such verses (e.g., 'Alone', 'To Isadore') accompanied by commentary on provenance, facsimile evidence, and stylistic assessment, leaving ultimate judgment to the reader.

You may copy it, give it away or re-use it under the terms of the Project Gutenberg™ License included with this eBook or online at www.gutenberg.org.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 1.E.1: The specific sentence (with active links to the full license) must appear prominently whenever a Project Gutenberg work is accessed or distributed. Failure to include it violates the license terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg: do not remove or detach the full license
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not unlink, detach, or remove the full Project Gutenberg License terms from the work or any files containing part of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 1.E.4–1.E.5: The full license must remain attached to redistributed copies and the required sentence must be prominently displayed. Alternate formats must include the full license; do not strip license text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg: provide original 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' copy on request
rubrics_metrics.description: If you distribute the work in a format other than the official format, you must, at no additional cost, provide a copy or means to obtain the original 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' (or the original official form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 1.E.6: Conversion and distribution in other formats are allowed, but the distributor must provide, on request and at no extra cost, a copy or means to export the work in its original official format and include the full license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg: restrictions on charging fees and required royalties for commercial redistribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not charge a fee for access unless you comply with the license's commercial-distribution provisions, including paying a 20% royalty in certain cases and providing refunds and defect remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraphs 1.E.7–1.E.9 and 1.E.8 specify that free distribution is the norm; charging is permitted only under strict conditions (20% gross profits royalty to the trademark owner, refund policies, compliance with other terms). If charging or distributing on different terms, obtain written permission from the Project Gutenberg Literary Archive Foundation.

rubrics_metrics.description: Project Gutenberg works may contain 'Defects' (transcription errors, incomplete data, etc.); the Foundation disclaims most liabilities and provides limited remedies as specified in the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 1.F.1–1.F.3: Disclose possible defects, include the warranty/disclaimer language, and follow the 'Right of Replacement or Refund' procedure if a defect is discovered within stated timeframes. Distributors and users accept the limited warranty/disclaimer terms.
